# Built-in checks

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_docs.py; do not edit by hand. -->

A check item names its check (`check: missing_periods`); the code (`TMP-004`)
is its stable audit ID in reports. Besides the settings listed here, every item
takes the common fields `name`, `severity`, `tags`, `enabled` and `description`.
Only the checks listing `where` take it; for the others, check a view
(`<dataset>.<view>`) or a dataset of the filtered rows. `qavf list-checks`
prints the same catalog.

## Comparison

### compare

**Datasets compare within tolerance** · code `CMP-001` · default severity `ERROR`

Each configured pair of datasets (for example two versions of an output) agrees after alignment (column mapping, lossless casts, unit conversion, recoding, derived columns, filters) at each configured level: structure, key coverage, keyed records, grouped measures, time, space, distributions, relationships and contributions to the change.

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `where` | `str \| None` | `None` | SQL condition: assess only the rows that match it. Only the checks that list ``where`` among their settings take it (``expression``, ``compare`` and plugins whose parameters declare it); for the others, check a view (``<dataset>.<view>``) or a dataset of the filtered rows. |
| `datasets` | `list[str]` | **required** | The datasets related; the reference first (by default). |
| `strategy` | `Literal['reference', 'sequential', 'all_pairs', 'consensus']` | `reference` | How the datasets are paired: the reference with each other (reference), each with the next (sequential), every pair (all_pairs) or each with the consensus of all (consensus). |
| `reference` | `str \| None` | `None` | The authoritative dataset (default: the first); with consensus, the dataset whose value breaks ties under ties: reference. |
| `max_pairs` | `int` | `28` | all_pairs refuses more pairs than this. |
| `consensus` | `ConsensusSettings \| None` | `None` | How the consensus is built (strategy consensus). |
| `keys` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` | Columns identifying a record on both sides (candidate names). Coverage and record levels need them. |
| `columns` | `dict[str, str]` | `{}` | Baseline columns renamed in the candidate (``baseline_name: candidate_name``). |
| `cast` | `dict[str, CastSpec]` | `{}` | Lossless type conversions; a value that would change makes the comparison not assessed. |
| `units` | `dict[str, UnitConversion]` | `{}` |  |
| `recode` | `dict[str, Recode]` | `{}` |  |
| `derive` | `dict[str, str]` | `{}` | New columns computed on both sides from a Polars SQL expression. |
| `steps` | `tuple[StepConfig, ...]` | `[]` | Further alignment steps, e.g. from plugins, applied after ``derive``. |
| `baseline_where` | `str \| None` | `None` | Compare only baseline rows matching this Polars SQL condition. |
| `candidate_where` | `str \| None` | `None` |  |
| `ignore_columns` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` |  |
| `rtol` | `float` | `1e-06` | Default relative tolerance for values and measures. |
| `atol` | `float` | `1e-09` |  |
| `tolerances` | `dict[str, ColumnTolerance]` | `{}` | Per-column tolerances, e.g. ``{share: {atol: 0.001}, code: {exact: true}}``. |
| `levels` | `tuple[LevelConfig, ...] \| None` | `None` | Levels to compare; ``structure, coverage, records`` (``structure`` without keys). |
| `min_rows` | `int` | `1` | Fewest aligned rows on each side for the comparison to be assessed. |
| `decision` | `Literal['material', 'significant', 'material_and_significant', 'equivalence']` | `material_and_significant` | How materiality and significance combine: ``material_and_significant`` (fail only when a difference is material and significant), ``material`` (no tests; for a core install without the stats extra), ``significant`` or ``equivalence`` (pass only when equivalence within the tolerance is shown). |
| `alpha` | `float` | `0.05` | Significance level, applied after the correction. |
| `correction` | `Literal['none', 'bonferroni', 'holm', 'bh', 'by']` | `bh` | Multiple-testing correction across each check's family (groups, buckets, series, columns): ``bh`` (Benjamini-Hochberg), ``by``, ``holm``, ``bonferroni`` or ``none``. |
| `seed` | `int` | `0` | Seed of resampling tests; the same seed reproduces a comparison exactly. |
| `max_work` | `int` | `20000000` | Largest work (resamples x values, or values collected) of one test; a larger test is not assessed rather than slow. |
| `chart_points` | `int` | `500` | Most per-member values (buckets, zones, contributions) a level keeps for the report's charts, within the evidence byte limit; 0 keeps none. |

#### `ConsensusSettings`

How the consensus of the members is built, key by key (``consensus:``).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numeric` | `Literal['median', 'mean', 'trimmed_mean']` | `median` | Consensus of a number: the median, the mean or the trimmed mean of the members. |
| `trim` | `float` | `0.1` | Fraction trimmed from each end for ``trimmed_mean``. |
| `categorical` | `Literal['majority', 'plurality']` | `majority` | Consensus of any other value: held by more than half of the members (``majority``), or by more members than any other value (``plurality``). |
| `min_agreement` | `float` | `0.5` | Share of the members holding a key that must agree for a consensus value; for numbers, the share that reports one. |
| `ties` | `Literal['report', 'reference']` | `report` | A tie leaves the key without a consensus value (``report``: not assessed for that key), or takes the reference member's value (``reference``). |

#### `CastSpec`

A lossless type conversion of one column (``{dtype: int}`` or just ``int``).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dtype` | `Literal['int', 'float', 'decimal', 'str', 'bool', 'date', 'datetime']` | **required** |  |
| `scale` | `int \| None` | `None` | Decimal places for ``dtype: decimal``. |
| `side` | `Literal['baseline', 'candidate', 'both']` | `both` | Which dataset's column is converted. |

#### `UnitConversion`

Multiply one side's column by ``factor`` so both sides share a unit.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `factor` | `int \| Decimal \| float` | **required** | Exact for integers and decimals; a float factor means its decimal spelling. |
| `side` | `Literal['baseline', 'candidate']` | `baseline` |  |
| `from_unit` | `str \| None` | `None` | The unit the column must be declared in (``schema.columns.<c>.unit``), if declared. |
| `to_unit` | `str \| None` | `None` | The unit after conversion, compared with the other side's declared unit. |

#### `Recode`

Replace categorical values, e.g. codes renamed between versions.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | `dict[str, Any] \| list[tuple[Any, Any]]` | **required** | ``old: new`` (mapping keys are text; they are converted to the column type) or a list of ``[old, new]`` pairs for typed old values. |
| `side` | `Literal['baseline', 'candidate', 'both']` | `baseline` |  |
| `unmapped` | `Literal['keep', 'null', 'error']` | `keep` | Values without a mapping: kept (when losslessly representable), made null, or reported (the comparison is then not assessed). |

#### `StepConfig`

A plugin (or built-in) alignment step: ``{step: name, ...its parameters}``.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | `str` | **required** |  |
| `params` | `dict[str, Any]` | `{}` |  |

#### `ColumnTolerance`

A tolerance for one column of a baseline comparison.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rtol` | `float \| None` | `None` | Relative tolerance; the baseline's (or rule's) when omitted. |
| `atol` | `float \| None` | `None` | Absolute tolerance; the baseline's (or rule's) when omitted. |
| `exact` | `bool` | `False` | Compare exactly (no tolerance), e.g. for identifiers or categorical codes. |

#### `LevelConfig`

A comparison level: ``records`` or ``{level: groups, group_by: [...], ...}``.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `str` | **required** |  |
| `name` | `str \| None` | `None` | Label in reports; the level name when omitted. |
| `severity` | `Severity \| None` | `None` | Severity of this level's failures; the rule's when omitted. |
| `params` | `dict[str, Any]` | `{}` |  |

*When it fails:* Decide whether each difference is intended. Start with structure and coverage (renamed, missing or new columns and keys), then the largest record and group changes. Map, convert or recode intended differences in the comparison.


## Input

### datasets_available

**Datasets available** · code `INP-001` · default severity `CRITICAL`

Required datasets are accessible and their schemas can be inspected; optional datasets may be absent. Native sources are not fully scanned by this availability check, so it does not certify that every source record can be parsed.

Comes from the dataset's `schema` (and its availability); it has no check item and runs wherever the contract is declared.

*When it fails:* Check the dataset's source settings (paths, queries, connection details) and confirm the upstream step that produces it completed. Mark a dataset 'required: false' if it is genuinely optional.

### schema

**Schema conformance** · code `INP-002` · default severity `CRITICAL`

Each dataset has its required columns with the declared types, no undeclared columns when strict, and a row count within the configured limits.

Comes from the dataset's `schema` (and its availability); it has no check item and runs wherever the contract is declared.

*When it fails:* Fix the step that produced the dataset so column names and types match the schema, or update the schema if the layout changed intentionally. A column read as text when another type is declared usually holds a few stray values: the listed rows show them. Declare placeholders such as 'N/A' in the column's missing_values. A code declared str but read as a number has lost its leading zeros: read it as text at the source ('text_columns' for CSV files).

### column_limits

**Column QA limits** · code `INP-003` · default severity `ERROR`

Column values respect their configured QA limits: nulls, bounds, allowed and forbidden values, patterns, lengths, uniqueness and aggregate statistics.

Comes from the dataset's `schema` (and its availability); it has no check item and runs wherever the contract is declared.

*When it fails:* Inspect the listed rows. Out-of-range values usually come from unit mix-ups, sign errors, sentinel values such as -999, or failed joins that leave nulls. If a value is legitimate, widen the limit or downgrade that check's severity.

### unique_keys

**Unique primary keys** · code `INP-004` · default severity `ERROR`

Each dataset's primary-key columns identify its rows uniquely.

Comes from the dataset's `schema` (and its availability); it has no check item and runs wherever the contract is declared.

*When it fails:* Duplicate keys double-count values when tables are joined. De-duplicate at the source, or add the missing dimension to the primary key.

### references

**Referential integrity** · code `INP-005` · default severity `ERROR`

Every configured foreign-key value exists in the referenced dataset. Keys are compared exactly; key types that cannot be compared exactly are reported.

Comes from the dataset's `schema` (and its availability); it has no check item and runs wherever the contract is declared.

*When it fails:* Orphaned keys are silently dropped by inner joins. Add the missing reference rows or correct the keys in the child dataset.

### expression

**Row expressions** · code `INP-006` · default severity `ERROR`

Every row satisfies the dataset's configured SQL expressions, e.g. 'pm25 <= pm10' or 'end_date >= start_date'.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `where` | `str \| None` | `None` | SQL condition: assess only the rows that match it. Only the checks that list ``where`` among their settings take it (``expression``, ``compare`` and plugins whose parameters declare it); for the others, check a view (``<dataset>.<view>``) or a dataset of the filtered rows. |
| `expr` | `str` | **required** | Condition every row satisfies, e.g. ``pm25 <= pm10``; it may query other datasets by name in subqueries. |
| `null_as` | `Literal['pass', 'fail']` | `pass` | How a row whose expression evaluates to NULL counts (SQL CHECK semantics: pass). |
| `min_applicable_rows` | `int` | `0` | With ``where``: fewer matching rows than this makes the check not assessed. |

*When it fails:* An expression failure means a relationship between columns that must always hold does not. Inspect the listed rows for mismatched units or rows combined from different sources.

### sql

**SQL assertions** · code `INP-007` · default severity `ERROR`

Each configured SQL assertion, a query that selects offending rows across any datasets, returns nothing.

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sql` | `str` | **required** | Query returning offending rows; every dataset is a table under its name. |

*When it fails:* Each returned row is a counter-example to the assertion. Run the assertion's query yourself to explore them.

### fresh

**Data freshness** · code `INP-008` · default severity `ERROR`

The newest value of each configured date or datetime column is no older than its max_age, measured from the run (or a configured reference time).

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `column` | `str` | **required** | A date or datetime column, e.g. a timestamp or reporting date. |
| `max_age` | `timedelta` | **required** | Largest acceptable age of the newest value, as an ISO 8601 duration (``P2D``, ``PT6H``) or seconds. |
| `max_future_skew` | `timedelta` | `datetime.timedelta(0)` | Largest allowed timestamp lead over the reference clock; defaults to zero. |
| `now` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | The reference time; the start of the run when omitted. Set it to re-check a past run reproducibly. A time without a time zone is UTC. |

*When it fails:* Stale data usually means an upstream job did not run or a file was not refreshed. Check the producing pipeline's last run before trusting downstream results.

### not_applicable

**Not-applicable values** · code `INP-009` · default severity `ERROR`

Declared N/A values are counted independently; configured groups are all or none N/A in each row.

Comes from the dataset's `schema` (and its availability); it has no check item and runs wherever the contract is declared.

*When it fails:* Make every column in the group applicable, or mark every column with its declared N/A token.


## Reconciliation

### totals_match

**Totals reconcile** · code `REC-001` · default severity `ERROR`

For each configured reconciliation, the sum (or row count) of one dataset equals that of another for every key, within tolerance: input-to-output conservation, published control totals, component sums.

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datasets` | `list[str]` | **required** | The datasets related; the reference first (by default). |
| `strategy` | `Literal['reference', 'sequential', 'all_pairs', 'consensus']` | `reference` | How the datasets are paired: the reference with each other (reference), each with the next (sequential), every pair (all_pairs) or each with the consensus of all (consensus). |
| `reference` | `str \| None` | `None` | The authoritative dataset (default: the first); with consensus, the dataset whose value breaks ties under ties: reference. |
| `max_pairs` | `int` | `28` | all_pairs refuses more pairs than this. |
| `consensus` | `ConsensusSettings \| None` | `None` | How the consensus is built (strategy consensus). |
| `value` | `str \| None` | `None` | Column to sum on both datasets; omit to count rows. |
| `keys` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Key columns totals are compared on. |
| `sides` | `dict[str, _SideSettings]` | `{}` | Per-dataset value or key overrides. |
| `rtol` | `float \| None` | `None` | Relative tolerance. Default: exact for row counts and integer totals, 1e-9 when a side sums floats (to allow ordinary measurement and representation differences). |
| `atol` | `float` | `0.0` |  |
| `missing_side` | `Literal['fail', 'ignore']` | `fail` | A key with a total on one side only: a violation (``fail``, the default) or left out (``ignore``, e.g. when the right side covers a subset). |
| `null_keys` | `Literal['fail', 'exempt']` | `fail` | Rows with a null key component cannot be attributed to a key: by default they make the reconciliation fail; ``exempt`` leaves them out (counted). |

#### `ConsensusSettings`

How the consensus of the members is built, key by key (``consensus:``).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numeric` | `Literal['median', 'mean', 'trimmed_mean']` | `median` | Consensus of a number: the median, the mean or the trimmed mean of the members. |
| `trim` | `float` | `0.1` | Fraction trimmed from each end for ``trimmed_mean``. |
| `categorical` | `Literal['majority', 'plurality']` | `majority` | Consensus of any other value: held by more than half of the members (``majority``), or by more members than any other value (``plurality``). |
| `min_agreement` | `float` | `0.5` | Share of the members holding a key that must agree for a consensus value; for numbers, the share that reports one. |
| `ties` | `Literal['report', 'reference']` | `report` | A tie leaves the key without a consensus value (``report``: not assessed for that key), or takes the reference member's value (``reference``). |

#### `SideSettings`

Per-dataset overrides of a two-dataset check.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `str \| None` | `None` |  |
| `keys` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` |  |

*When it fails:* A total that does not reconcile means rows were lost, duplicated or re-attributed between the two datasets. Start with the keys missing on one side, then the largest differences.

### shares

**Shares sum to total** · code `REC-002` · default severity `ERROR`

Within each group, the configured share column sums to its total (1 or 100) within an absolute tolerance.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `str` | **required** |  |
| `group_by` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` |  |
| `total` | `int \| Decimal \| float` | `1.0` | What each group's shares must sum to (1.0 for fractions, 100 for percent). |
| `atol` | `float` | `1e-06` |  |
| `missing` | `Literal['fail', 'ignore']` | `fail` | A missing share makes its group's sum unknowable: a violation by default. |

*When it fails:* Shares that do not sum to their total usually mean a missing category, a duplicated row, or shares normalised over a different set of groups.

### key_grid

**Complete key grid** · code `REC-003` · default severity `ERROR`

Each configured dataset contains every combination of its dimensions' expected values (e.g. county x year x pollutant), optionally no others and no repeats.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dimensions` | `dict[str, Dimension]` | **required** |  |
| `unexpected` | `bool` | `False` | Also report combinations present but not expected. |
| `unique` | `bool` | `False` | Each combination must occur at most once. |

#### `Dimension`

The expected values of one key column: listed, or taken from a reference.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | `tuple[Any, ...] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `from_dataset` | `str \| None` | `None` | A reference dataset whose distinct values of the same-named column are expected. |

*When it fails:* A missing combination is silently treated as zero by most downstream sums. Re-run the producing step for the missing keys, or narrow the expected values.

### key_sets_match

**Key sets match** · code `REC-004` · default severity `ERROR`

Each configured pair of datasets has identical sets of (non-null) keys: every key of one exists in the other, in both directions.

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datasets` | `list[str]` | **required** | The datasets related; the reference first (by default). |
| `strategy` | `Literal['reference', 'sequential', 'all_pairs', 'consensus']` | `reference` | How the datasets are paired: the reference with each other (reference), each with the next (sequential), every pair (all_pairs) or each with the consensus of all (consensus). |
| `reference` | `str \| None` | `None` | The authoritative dataset (default: the first); with consensus, the dataset whose value breaks ties under ties: reference. |
| `max_pairs` | `int` | `28` | all_pairs refuses more pairs than this. |
| `consensus` | `ConsensusSettings \| None` | `None` | How the consensus is built (strategy consensus). |
| `keys` | `list[str]` | **required** | Key columns compared on both datasets. |
| `sides` | `dict[str, _SideSettings]` | `{}` | Per-dataset key overrides. |

#### `ConsensusSettings`

How the consensus of the members is built, key by key (``consensus:``).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numeric` | `Literal['median', 'mean', 'trimmed_mean']` | `median` | Consensus of a number: the median, the mean or the trimmed mean of the members. |
| `trim` | `float` | `0.1` | Fraction trimmed from each end for ``trimmed_mean``. |
| `categorical` | `Literal['majority', 'plurality']` | `majority` | Consensus of any other value: held by more than half of the members (``majority``), or by more members than any other value (``plurality``). |
| `min_agreement` | `float` | `0.5` | Share of the members holding a key that must agree for a consensus value; for numbers, the share that reports one. |
| `ties` | `Literal['report', 'reference']` | `report` | A tie leaves the key without a consensus value (``report``: not assessed for that key), or takes the reference member's value (``reference``). |

#### `SideSettings`

Per-dataset overrides of a two-dataset check.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `str \| None` | `None` |  |
| `keys` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` |  |

*When it fails:* Keys on one side only mean rows were dropped or invented between the two datasets; a one-directional foreign key would not notice the other direction.

### batch_consistent

**Consistent batch** · code `REC-005` · default severity `ERROR`

Each configured group of datasets carries a single, identical value in its batch column (run id, export id, watermark), so they come from one consistent extract.

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datasets` | `tuple[str, ...]` | **required** |  |
| `column` | `str` | **required** | The batch identifier column each dataset carries (e.g. ``run_id``, ``as_of``). |

*When it fails:* Datasets from different batches were read while an upstream job was updating them. Re-extract them together (or use a connection snapshot) before comparing.


## Regression

### matches_baseline

**Outputs match baseline** · code `REG-001` · default severity `ERROR`

Generated outputs equal their stored baselines row-for-row by key, within the configured numeric tolerance.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `str \| None` | `None` | Baseline file; relative paths resolve against the configuration file. |
| `source` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Any source specification instead of ``path``, e.g. a baseline database table. |
| `keys` | `tuple[str, ...]` | **required** |  |
| `rtol` | `float \| None` | `None` |  |
| `atol` | `float \| None` | `None` |  |
| `ignore_columns` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` |  |
| `schema` | `Literal['compatible', 'strict', 'ignore']` | `compatible` | ``schema`` in configuration. How column types are compared: ``compatible`` reports changes of kind (number to text, date to datetime, a time zone added), ``strict`` any dtype change, ``ignore`` none. |
| `columns` | `dict[str, ColumnTolerance]` | `{}` | Per-column tolerances, e.g. ``{share: {atol: 0.001}, code: {exact: true}}``, so one mixed-unit table needs no globally loose tolerance. |
| `rename` | `dict[str, str]` | `{}` | Baseline columns renamed in the output (``baseline_name: output_name``). The baseline is compared under output names, which ``keys``, ``ignore_columns`` and ``columns`` use. A mapped column the baseline lacks makes the check not assessed. |
| `max_differences` | `int` | `1000` |  |
| `require_manifest` | `bool` | `False` | Only compare against baseline files accepted with a manifest (``qavf baseline``): a baseline without one is not used, so an unreviewed file cannot become the reference. |

#### `ColumnTolerance`

A tolerance for one column of a baseline comparison.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rtol` | `float \| None` | `None` | Relative tolerance; the baseline's (or rule's) when omitted. |
| `atol` | `float \| None` | `None` | Absolute tolerance; the baseline's (or rule's) when omitted. |
| `exact` | `bool` | `False` | Compare exactly (no tolerance), e.g. for identifiers or categorical codes. |

*When it fails:* Decide whether the change is intended. If a code or input change explains it, review the differences and refresh the baseline (qavf baseline). If not, the utility has regressed: bisect recent changes using the listed keys.


## Spatial

### coordinates

**Coordinate validity** · code `GEO-001` · default severity `ERROR`

Latitudes lie in [-90, 90] and longitudes in [-180, 180], coordinates are present and finite, not (0, 0), inside the configured bounding box and, with 'within', inside the polygons of a zone layer or study area.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | `str` | `latitude` |  |
| `longitude` | `str` | `longitude` |  |
| `bbox` | `BoundingBox \| None` | `None` | Points outside this box are violations (e.g. the study area). |
| `allow_missing` | `bool` | `False` | Rows without coordinates are allowed (by default they are violations). |
| `null_island` | `bool` | `True` | Flag (0, 0), the usual sign of a missing value written as zero. |
| `within` | `ZoneLayer \| None` | `None` | Points must fall inside these polygons (a zone layer or study area, in EPSG:4326 or transformed from its ``crs``); valid points outside are violations of a separate ``within`` check. Needs DuckDB's spatial extension. |
| `boundary` | `Literal['intersects', 'contains']` | `intersects` | Whether a point on the boundary of ``within`` is inside (``intersects``). |
| `assignment_limits` | `AssignmentLimits` | `{'batch_size': 16384, 'max_points': 1000000, 'max_matches': 2000000, 'max_work': 20000000}` | Point, match and work admission for ``within``; ordinary checks use the defaults. |

#### `BoundingBox`

The area all points must fall in (inclusive), in degrees.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_lat` | `int \| Decimal \| float` | **required** |  |
| `max_lat` | `int \| Decimal \| float` | **required** |  |
| `min_lon` | `int \| Decimal \| float` | **required** |  |
| `max_lon` | `int \| Decimal \| float` | **required** |  |

#### `ZoneLayer`

Zone polygons: ``{dataset: name}`` or ``{path: file}``, with an ``id`` column.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset` | `str \| None` | `None` | A configured dataset holding the zones (an id and a WKB or WKT geometry column). |
| `path` | `str \| None` | `None` | A local GeoParquet, GeoJSON, shapefile or other ``ST_Read`` file (relative to the configuration). |
| `id` | `str` | `zone` | Zone id column. |
| `geometry` | `str \| None` | `None` | Geometry column: ``geometry`` for datasets and GeoParquet, ``geom`` for ``ST_Read``. |
| `crs` | `str` | `EPSG:4326` | CRS of the polygons; a file declaring another one is refused. |
| `layer` | `str \| None` | `None` | Layer of a multi-layer file (``ST_Read``'s ``layer``). |
| `repair` | `bool` | `False` | Replace invalid geometries with ``ST_MakeValid`` (recorded) instead of refusing them. |

#### `AssignmentLimits`

Finite row/work admission for point assignment, rather than an RSS ceiling.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_size` | `int` | `16384` | Maximum distinct points transformed together and selected rows per Arrow batch. |
| `max_points` | `int` | `1000000` | Maximum distinct point keys retained; excess points refuse the whole assignment. |
| `max_matches` | `int` | `2000000` | Maximum selected point-zone mappings retained, including ``overlap: all`` expansion. |
| `max_work` | `int` | `20000000` | Maximum bounding-box candidate pairs admitted across batches, before exact tests. |

*When it fails:* Out-of-range latitudes usually mean latitude and longitude were swapped, or a projected coordinate (metres) was stored as degrees; (0, 0) is almost always a missing location written as zero.

### entity_outliers

**Entity outlier detection** · code `SPA-001` · default severity `WARNING`

Within each group, no entity's (normalised) metric is a statistical outlier relative to the other entities (z-score, modified z-score or IQR).

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metric` | `Inline_metric_entity_outliers \| str` | **required** | The metric examined: the name of one the dataset defines under metrics (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `method` | `OutlierMethod` | `modified_zscore` |  |
| `threshold` | `float \| None` | `None` | Method threshold; the conventional default for the method when omitted. |
| `min_entities` | `int` | `5` | Fewest entities in a group for outlier detection to be attempted. |
| `min_relative_deviation` | `float` | `0.1` | An entity is only flagged if it also differs from the group median by at least this fraction. Stops tightly clustered groups, where any tiny spread is 'statistically' extreme, from producing immaterial findings. |

#### Inline `metric` definition



| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `str` | **required** | Numeric column. |
| `group_by` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` | Columns to break the metric down by. |
| `aggregate` | `Literal['sum', 'mean', 'count', 'min', 'max', 'first', 'last', 'weighted_mean', 'none']` | `sum` |  |
| `weight` | `str \| None` | `None` | Weight column for ``weighted_mean``. |
| `order_by` | `str \| tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` | Column or lexicographic column list for ``first``/``last``. Conflicting values tied at the selected key are rejected; add an explicit tie-break column. |
| `entity` | `str` | **required** | Column identifying the entity (county, site, link, …). |
| `per` | `Normalizer \| None \| str` | `None` | Normalizer: ``<dataset>.<column>`` (e.g. ``counts.aadt``), or a mapping with ``dataset``, ``value``, ``on`` and ``aggregate``. |

#### `Normalizer`

Denominator for a metric, combined (``aggregate``, a sum by default) to the keys

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset` | `str` | **required** |  |
| `value` | `str` | **required** |  |
| `on` | `tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` | Columns to join the denominator on; the metric's keys the denominator also has when omitted. Set it so a renamed or extra column cannot change the join grain. |
| `aggregate` | `Literal['sum', 'mean', 'count', 'min', 'max', 'first', 'last', 'weighted_mean', 'none']` | `sum` |  |
| `weight` | `str \| None` | `None` |  |
| `order_by` | `str \| tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` |  |

*When it fails:* Check the outlying entity's inputs first. An entity that is an outlier on every metric usually has a denominator (activity) problem; one that is an outlier on a single metric has a problem specific to that measure.

Each entity's (normalised) metric stays within a configured factor of the median of its group.

Denominator for a metric, combined (``aggregate``, a sum by default) to the keys

### coverage

**Entity coverage** · code `SPA-003` · default severity `ERROR`

Each dataset with the entity column contains every expected entity, in every period when a time column is configured.

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | `str \| None` | `None` | Column identifying entities; the rule skips until this is set. |
| `time_column` | `str \| None` | `None` | When set (and present), coverage is checked separately for every period. |
| `expected_periods` | `tuple[Any, ...] \| None` | `None` | Periods every time-indexed dataset must cover; the union of periods found across the checked datasets when omitted. |
| `expected_entities` | `tuple[Any, ...] \| None` | `None` | Entities every dataset must cover. When omitted: the entities of ``reference_dataset`` if set, otherwise the union across datasets. |
| `reference` | `str \| None` | `None` | Authoritative entity list (e.g. a site inventory), read from its entity column. |
| `zone_layer` | `ZoneLayer \| None` | `None` | Expected entities are the ids of this zone layer (``{dataset: zones, id: taz}`` or ``{path: zones.geojson, id: taz}``); only ``ST_Read`` files need DuckDB's spatial extension. |
| `datasets` | `tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` |  |
| `require_time_column` | `bool` | `False` | With ``time_column``: a checked dataset without it is not assessed, instead of being checked for entities only (so losing the column cannot weaken the check). |
| `unexpected_entities` | `bool` | `False` | Also report entities that are not expected (with ``expected_entities``, ``reference_dataset`` or ``zone_layer``): coverage then means the same set, not only a superset. |

#### `ZoneLayer`

Zone polygons: ``{dataset: name}`` or ``{path: file}``, with an ``id`` column.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset` | `str \| None` | `None` | A configured dataset holding the zones (an id and a WKB or WKT geometry column). |
| `path` | `str \| None` | `None` | A local GeoParquet, GeoJSON, shapefile or other ``ST_Read`` file (relative to the configuration). |
| `id` | `str` | `zone` | Zone id column. |
| `geometry` | `str \| None` | `None` | Geometry column: ``geometry`` for datasets and GeoParquet, ``geom`` for ``ST_Read``. |
| `crs` | `str` | `EPSG:4326` | CRS of the polygons; a file declaring another one is refused. |
| `layer` | `str \| None` | `None` | Layer of a multi-layer file (``ST_Read``'s ``layer``). |
| `repair` | `bool` | `False` | Replace invalid geometries with ``ST_MakeValid`` (recorded) instead of refusing them. |

*When it fails:* An entity missing from one dataset but present in others is dropped by joins and understates totals. Add its rows, or list 'expected_entities' explicitly if the study area is narrower than the data.


## Statistical

### outliers

**Statistical outliers in values** · code `STA-001` · default severity `WARNING`

Within each configured group, no individual value is an outlier by the configured method (z-score, modified z-score or IQR) and threshold.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `column` | `str` | **required** | Numeric column. |
| `group_by` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` | Columns to break the metric down by. |
| `method` | `OutlierMethod \| None` | `None` | Overrides the rule-level method for this target. |
| `threshold` | `float \| None` | `None` | Overrides the rule-level threshold for this target. |
| `direction` | `Literal['both', 'high', 'low']` | `both` | Flag only unusually high (or low) values, e.g. spikes in a count. |
| `min_relative_deviation` | `float` | `0.0` | Also require the value to differ from its group's median by at least this fraction (0.1 = 10 %), so statistically extreme but immaterial values pass. |
| `transform` | `Literal['none', 'log']` | `none` | Scan ``log(value)``: for skewed, multiplicative data (concentrations, flows). Non-positive values cannot be transformed and are reported as not tested. |
| `min_group_size` | `int` | `8` | Groups with fewer non-null values are not scanned. |

*When it fails:* Outliers are prompts for review, not proof of error. Inspect the flagged rows; if they are legitimate, group more finely or raise the threshold for that target so the check stays informative.

### drift

**Distribution drift** · code `STA-002` · default severity `WARNING`

Each configured column's distribution stays close to a reference dataset's, by population stability index or a two-sample KS test (with a minimum sample size, an effect-size floor and a Bonferroni correction across KS comparisons).

Goes in top-level `checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datasets` | `list[str]` | **required** | The datasets related; the reference first (by default). |
| `strategy` | `Literal['reference', 'sequential', 'all_pairs', 'consensus']` | `reference` | How the datasets are paired: the reference with each other (reference), each with the next (sequential), every pair (all_pairs) or each with the consensus of all (consensus). |
| `reference` | `str \| None` | `None` | The authoritative dataset (default: the first); with consensus, the dataset whose value breaks ties under ties: reference. |
| `max_pairs` | `int` | `28` | all_pairs refuses more pairs than this. |
| `consensus` | `ConsensusSettings \| None` | `None` | How the consensus is built (strategy consensus). |
| `column` | `str` | **required** |  |
| `method` | `Literal['psi', 'ks']` | `psi` | ``psi``: population stability index over the reference's quantile bins (numbers) or categories (text). ``ks``: two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (numbers; needs the stats extra). |
| `bins` | `int` | `10` |  |
| `max_psi` | `float` | `0.2` | PSI above which the distribution has drifted (0.1 small, 0.2 notable, 0.25 large). |
| `alpha` | `float` | `0.01` | KS significance level before the multiple-testing correction. |
| `min_effect` | `float` | `0.1` | KS statistic below which a significant difference is still immaterial (large samples make tiny differences significant). |
| `min_samples` | `int` | `50` | Fewest usable values on each side for a comparison to be judged. |
| `correction` | `Literal['none', 'bonferroni', 'holm', 'bh', 'by']` | `bonferroni` | Multiple-testing correction across the KS comparisons (``holm``, ``bh``, ``by``, ``none``); a comparison drifts when its adjusted p-value is below its ``alpha``. |

#### `ConsensusSettings`

How the consensus of the members is built, key by key (``consensus:``).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numeric` | `Literal['median', 'mean', 'trimmed_mean']` | `median` | Consensus of a number: the median, the mean or the trimmed mean of the members. |
| `trim` | `float` | `0.1` | Fraction trimmed from each end for ``trimmed_mean``. |
| `categorical` | `Literal['majority', 'plurality']` | `majority` | Consensus of any other value: held by more than half of the members (``majority``), or by more members than any other value (``plurality``). |
| `min_agreement` | `float` | `0.5` | Share of the members holding a key that must agree for a consensus value; for numbers, the share that reports one. |
| `ties` | `Literal['report', 'reference']` | `report` | A tie leaves the key without a consensus value (``report``: not assessed for that key), or takes the reference member's value (``reference``). |

*When it fails:* Drift is not an error by itself: the population may really have changed. Check what changed upstream (inputs, coverage, units) before accepting the new run.


## Temporal

### change_rate

**Period-over-period change within bounds** · code `TMP-001` · default severity `WARNING`

The compound change per time unit between consecutive periods stays within the configured threshold for each series.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | `Inline_series_change_rate \| str` | **required** | The series examined: the name of one the dataset defines under series (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `max` | `float` | `0.25` | Largest accepted compound change per time unit, as a fraction (0.25 = 25 % per year when the time column holds years). |
| `min_value` | `float` | `0.0` | Ignore steps where both values are at or below this magnitude. |

#### Inline `series` definition



| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `str` | **required** | Numeric column. |
| `group_by` | `tuple[str, ...]` | `[]` | Columns to break the metric down by. |
| `aggregate` | `Literal['sum', 'mean', 'count', 'min', 'max', 'first', 'last', 'weighted_mean', 'none']` | `sum` |  |
| `weight` | `str \| None` | `None` | Weight column for ``weighted_mean``. |
| `order_by` | `str \| tuple[str, ...] \| None` | `None` | Column or lexicographic column list for ``first``/``last``. Conflicting values tied at the selected key are rejected; add an explicit tie-break column. |
| `bucket` | `Bucket \| None` | `None` | Calendar bucket or cyclic profile of a Date/Datetime time column (``day``, ``15 minutes``, ``month``, ``hour_of_day``, ...). Without it, time values are used as they are (a numeric period such as a year). |
| `time_zone` | `str \| None` | `None` | IANA zone of the local calendar: naive times are wall-clock times there, aware times are converted to it. Aware columns default to their own zone. |
| `time_format` | `str \| None` | `None` | ``strftime`` format for parsing a text time column (unparseable values are reported, never dropped). |
| `time_column` | `str` | `year` | Numeric time column (e.g. a year), or a Date, Datetime or text column with ``bucket``. Rates of change are per unit of it (per bucket of the exact bucket sequence when bucketed); seasons use the local calendar slot. |
| `expected_trend` | `Literal['increasing', 'decreasing'] \| None` | `None` | Direction the series should move in; used by the trend-direction rule. |

#### `Bucket`

A calendar bucket (``day``, ``15 minutes``, ``6h``) or a cyclic profile (``season``).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | `Literal['second', 'minute', 'hour', 'day', 'week', 'month', 'quarter', 'year', 'hour_of_day', 'day_of_week', 'day_of_year', 'month_of_year', 'quarter_of_year', 'season']` | **required** | ``second``, ``minute``, ``hour``, ``day``, ``week``, ``month``, ``quarter``, ``year``, or a profile: ``hour_of_day``, ``day_of_week``, ``day_of_year``, ``month_of_year``, ``quarter_of_year``, ``season``. |
| `every` | `int` | `1` | Multiple of a calendar unit (``{unit: minute, every: 15}``). |
| `week_start` | `Literal['monday', 'tuesday', 'wednesday', 'thursday', 'friday', 'saturday', 'sunday']` | `monday` | First day of a ``week`` bucket, and of the ``day_of_week`` order. |
| `hemisphere` | `Literal['north', 'south']` | `north` | Names of the meteorological seasons (December-February is winter in the north). |
| `seasons` | `dict[str, tuple[int, ...]] \| None` | `None` | Custom seasons, ``name: [months]`` in cycle order, covering each month once. |

*When it fails:* Review the flagged steps against known drivers. A jump in one group only usually means an input for that period was swapped, duplicated or left at a default.

#### `Bucket`

| `seasons` | `dict[str, tuple[int, ...]] \| None` | `None` | Custom seasons, ``name: [months]`` in cycle order, covering each month once. |

### trend_outliers

**Trend consistency** · code `TMP-003` · default severity `WARNING`

No period is both a statistically significant outlier from its series' fitted trend (OLS of value on time, Bonferroni-adjusted studentized residuals) and materially off that trend.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | `Inline_series_trend_outliers \| str` | **required** | The series examined: the name of one the dataset defines under series (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `min_points` | `int` | `5` | Fewest periods needed to fit and test a trend. |
| `alpha` | `float` | `0.05` | Significance level of the corrected (Bonferroni by default) studentized-residual outlier test. |
| `min_relative_deviation` | `float` | `0.05` | A period is only flagged if it also departs from the fitted trend by at least this fraction, so statistically detectable but immaterial wobbles on a near-perfect trend are not reported. |
| `log_transform` | `bool` | `True` | Fit the trend on log(value) when every value is positive (multiplicative change). |
| `correction` | `Literal['none', 'bonferroni', 'holm', 'bh', 'by']` | `bonferroni` | Multiple-testing correction of the residual p-values within each series (``holm``, ``bh``, ``by``, ``none``). |

### missing_periods

**No missing periods** · code `TMP-004` · default severity `ERROR`

Each series group (for example each county and pollutant) has a value for every period.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | `Inline_series_missing_periods \| str` | **required** | The series examined: the name of one the dataset defines under series (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `expected` | `tuple[int \| Decimal \| float \| datetime \| date, ...] \| None` | `None` | Periods every group must have; the union of observed periods when omitted. For a bucketed series these are dates or datetimes (each names its bucket), and when omitted every bucket between the first and last observed one is expected. |
| `max_expected_periods` | `int` | `1000000` | Largest calendar grid of a bucketed series; a longer one is not assessed. |
| `expected_groups` | `tuple[dict[str, Any], ...] \| None` | `None` | Group combinations that must exist (``{county: 48001, pollutant: 2}``), so a group missing altogether is reported, not only gaps in groups that exist. |
| `groups_from` | `str \| None` | `None` | A dataset whose distinct combinations of each series' ``group_by`` columns are expected (e.g. an inventory of county x pollutant). |

### stale_values

**Stale or repeated values** · code `TMP-005` · default severity `WARNING`

No group of a series keeps the same value for max_repeats consecutive periods, and no period repeats the previous period's values in every group.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | `Inline_series_stale_values \| str` | **required** | The series examined: the name of one the dataset defines under series (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `max_repeats` | `int` | `3` | A run of this many (or more) consecutive periods with the same value is flagged: a stuck sensor, a value carried forward, an input that stopped updating. |
| `atol` | `float` | `0.0` | Values within this absolute difference count as the same. |
| `ignore_values` | `tuple[int \| Decimal \| float, ...]` | `[]` | Values that may legitimately stay constant (e.g. ``0`` for a closed site). |
| `copied_periods` | `bool` | `True` | Also flag a period in which every group (at least two) has exactly the previous period's values: an output copied forward instead of recomputed. |

### seasonal

**Seasonal anomalies** · code `TMP-007` · default severity `WARNING`

Each value is compared with the values of the same season (month, quarter, weekday) in the other cycles of its group; robust outliers are flagged.

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | `Inline_series_seasonal \| str` | **required** | The series examined: the name of one the dataset defines under series (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `season_length` | `int` | `12` | Periods per cycle: 12 for monthly data indexed 1..12 or as a running month number, 4 for quarters, 7 for days of the week. The season of a period is ``period mod season_length``; for a bucketed series the period is its local calendar position, so monthly buckets with 12 give calendar months and hourly buckets with 24 the local hour, unchanged by DST. |
| `threshold` | `float` | `3.5` | Modified z-score (median/MAD) above which a value is anomalous for its season. |
| `min_cycles` | `int` | `4` | Fewest values of a season (one per cycle) needed to judge it. |
| `min_relative_deviation` | `float` | `0.1` | Also require this relative difference from the season median. |

### level_shift

**Level shifts** · code `TMP-008` · default severity `WARNING`

No group of a series changes to a sustained new level: the best split into two segments does not separate their medians by more than the threshold (a robust screen, not a formal change-point test).

Goes in `datasets.<name>.checks`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | `Inline_series_level_shift \| str` | **required** | The series examined: the name of one the dataset defines under series (``other.name`` for another dataset's), or the definition itself. |
| `max_work` | `int` | `20000000` | Maximum observations processed across exact candidate splits for the whole rule. A group exceeding the remaining budget is explicitly unassessed; no approximate answer is substituted. Work across all configured groups and series is charged. |
| `min_segment` | `int` | `4` | Fewest periods on each side of a candidate shift. |
| `threshold` | `float` | `5.0` | Shift in medians, in units of the pooled robust spread (1.4826 x MAD of the values around their segment medians), above which a series is flagged. |
| `min_relative_shift` | `float` | `0.2` | Also require the medians to differ by this fraction of the earlier median. |
